title: Strict quotient shift squares and their normalized Roos realization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$, $n\ge1$. On the small pro-etale sites of finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ put $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be strict quotient-semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves, with ordinary unbounded derived categories, reduction $\mathcal R_W$ and total limit $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Use the simultaneous ringed-diagram models, exact inverse image $P_v$ for separated finite-type $v$, total derived direct image $S_p$ for proper $p$, exact extension by zero $J_j$ for quasi-compact open $j$, and derived system tensor [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Use the cochain convention $C[r]^i=C^{i+r}$, $d_{C[r]}=(-1)^rd_C$, and the prescribed comparisons [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data].

Take derived-complete constructible integral inputs $K_i$. Every input and intermediate system is normalized, has compatible etale-origin witnesses and constructible cohomology, and has cohomological and finite Tor amplitudes in common finite intervals. For a single operation $A=P_v,S_p,J_j$ or tensor, put $F_A(K_i)=\mathcal L A(\mathcal R K_i)$ and let $G_A(K_i)$ be its completed integral counterpart. Let $d_A:F_A(K_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_A(K_i)$ be the specified single-operation comparison [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence]. Use its actual whole-tower models: the quotient-complex comparisons $r_F,r_T$ [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison], the defining proper-image tower realization [lem-sf-primitive-reduction-transpose], and $d_j=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\mathcal L(r_j(K))^{-1}$ [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. For a restricted strict tower $X$ let $\mathsf C(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod X_n\to\prod X_n)[-1]$, $s((x_n))=(t_nx_{n+1})$, and use the normalized natural isomorphism $\rho_X:\mathsf C(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim X$ [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison].

For every integer $r$ and chosen input slot, the actual quotient-level comparison diagrams defining these $d_A$ admit simultaneous resolving representatives whose shift squares commute as strict chain-map diagrams, including every quotient transition. The maps in these squares are reindexed scalar-reduction and degree-zero operation maps; in a tensor slot their comparison is $t_{r,0}$ with coefficient $1$ or $t_{0,r}$ with coefficient $(-1)^{ri}$ on first degree $i$. In the open case this assertion includes the strict square for the specified $r_j$ on a flat-term K-flat reduction representative.

Under termwise product identifications, write $\chi_{X,r}:\mathsf C(X[r])\to\mathsf C(X)[r]$ for $(b,a)\mapsto(b,(-1)^ra)$ in the order (unshifted product, shifted product). For every tower comparison $f:X\to Y$ in the preceding strict diagrams, the normalized cone square satisfies
$$\chi_{Y,r}\,\mathsf C(f[r])=\mathsf C(f)[r]\,\chi_{X,r}.$$
After the corresponding signed tensor identifications, the analogous square holds for either shifted tensor slot. Through $\rho$, these are the squares for the actual total-limit morphisms. With $K_i^{(r)}$ denoting replacement of the chosen input by $K_i[r]$, and $\sigma_F:F_A(K_i^{(r)})\to F_A(K_i)[r]$, $\sigma_G:G_A(K_i^{(r)})\to G_A(K_i)[r]$ the specified operation/reduction/total-limit comparisons, they give the derived identity
$$\sigma_G\,d_A(K_i^{(r)})=d_A(K_i)[r]\,\sigma_F.$$
For open extension this identity uses the actual shift-compatible reconstruction unit of [lem-pur-reduction-limit-shift-adjunction]. All identities are independent of resolving representatives and natural in the input morphisms; the final identity is in the whole integral derived category, before taking cohomology or evaluating finite reductions.

proof.text: Choose good flat-term K-flat integral representatives $Q_i$ and the whole quotient systems $D(Q_i)_n=Q_i\otimes A_n$. Such representatives exist by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-quotient-system-flat-models] these compute coherent reduction, system pullback and system tensor, with the actual quotient transitions; by [lem-pur-sequence-kflat-comparison-shifts] the representative of a shifted reduction is $D(Q_i[r])=D(Q_i)[r]$, with identity comparison on the reindexed terms. Use the simultaneous operation resolutions of [lem-pur-basic-system-shift-resolution-calculus]. For proper image, choose the shifted K-injective system resolution $M[r]\to I[r]$ when $M\to I$ is used for $M$; the comparison is the degreewise equality $p_*I[r]=(p_*I)[r]$. No K-injectivity of individual reductions or of a scalar-restricted system is inferred. The hypotheses on schemes and coefficients in those nodes hold here; the common finite intervals may be shifted by $-r$, which is still a finite interval. This constructs compatible operation and reduction representatives for every single integer $r$.

source.place: Maps-used sentence, coefficient comparisons: simultaneous quotient and operation resolutions; Stacks 011G (definition-shift-cochain).

proof.text: On these models, scalar reduction sends a cochain map $f$ to $f^i\otimes1$ and a quotient transition to $1\otimes(A_{n+1}\to A_n)$, both of degree zero. Thus shifting first and then applying either map gives exactly its component in degree $i+r$. The same calculation applies to exact inverse image and degreewise direct image. For tensor use the comparisons of [lem-pur-basic-system-shift-resolution-calculus]: $t_{r,0}(x\otimes y)=x\otimes y$, while $t_{0,r}(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{ri}x\otimes y$ on first degree $i$. Every tensor comparison or quotient transition in these diagrams preserves the two degrees; its two routes therefore have the same coefficient $1$, respectively $(-1)^{ri}$. This proves strict commutation on the whole quotient systems, not merely equality of their derived evaluations. The cited node also supplies the chain-map property for the total tensor differential. The comparisons $r_F,r_T$ and the proper-image realization are precisely these whole-tower models by [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison] and [lem-sf-primitive-reduction-transpose]; hence no independently chosen finite-level arrows enter the argument.

source.place: Maps-used sentence, quotient-complex comparison maps for pullback, tensor and proper image.

proof.text: For the open case use [lem-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model], which supplies a flat-term K-flat $j_!Q$ and the strict system chain map $r_Q$. On each presheaf generator its formula is $[x]\otimes a\mapsto[x\otimes a|_U]$, with $a$ in degree zero. Applied to $x\in Q^{i+r}$ this formula is unchanged by shifting; the differentials on both sides acquire the same factor $(-1)^r$. The quotient transition replaces $a$ by its image in $A_n$ on either route, so the square also commutes with every transition before sheafification and afterwards. The localization of this same $r_Q$ is the specified $r_j$ by [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Thus the required open square concerns the actual comparison, with no faithfulness claim for derived evaluation.

source.place: Maps-used sentence, open tensor coefficient comparison and its strict quotient transitions.

proof.text: Put $h_X=1-s_X$ and $P_X=\prod_nX_n$. In the coordinate order of the statement, $\mathsf C(X)^i=P_X^i\oplus P_X^{i-1}$ and $d(b,a)=(db,-da-h_Xb)$. For $\epsilon=(-1)^r$, the source differential on $\mathsf C(X[r])$ is $(\epsilon db,-\epsilon da-h_Xb)$. Applying $\chi(b,a)=(b,\epsilon a)$ gives $(\epsilon db,-da-\epsilon h_Xb)$, exactly the target differential on $\mathsf C(X)[r]$ applied to $(b,\epsilon a)$. Its inverse has the same formula. For a strict tower map $f$, write $u=\prod_nf_n$. Strict transition compatibility gives $u h_X=h_Yu$ by taking each product projection, and $\mathsf C(f)(b,a)=(ub,ua)$. Both routes of the claimed cone square are consequently $(ub,\epsilon ua)$. The tensor-slot squares of Step 2 are strictly commuting tower squares, so the same calculation applies to them after their $t_{r,0}$ or $t_{0,r}$ identifications. The product/shift and cone normalization is the prescribed one in [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data].

source.place: Maps-used sentence, passage through the functorial Roos cone; Stacks 011G and 014E (definition-cone), explicit diagonal computation.

proof.text: Pass to actual total limits using the normalized $\rho$ of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. Countable products are exact on these pro-etale module sites by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], as required there. For a tower resolution $a:X\to I$, use $a[r]$ for the shifted tower. The preceding cone square applies to $a$. By [lem-pur-injective-tower-roos-shifts], the zero-shifted-coordinate inclusion $\eta_I:\lim I\to\mathsf C(I)$ satisfies $\chi_{I,r}\eta_{I[r]}=\eta_I[r]$. Hence in the formula $\rho_X=\eta_I^{-1}\mathsf C(a)$, the cone squares for $a$ and the displayed square for $\eta$ give $\sigma_{\lim}\rho_{X[r]}=\rho_X[r]\chi_{X,r}$. This identifies the cone comparison with the prescribed right-derived total-limit comparison on all strict towers. For semilinear systems the additional K-injective replacement after scalar restriction uses exactly the shifted replacement by [lem-pur-sequence-kinjective-comparison-shifts]; no preservation of K-injectives under scalar restriction is needed. Naturality of $\rho$ now turns the strict squares of Steps 2-4 into the squares of the actual total-limit maps.

source.place: Maps-used sentence, normalized total-limit realization; Stacks 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), shifted K-injective inclusion.

proof.text: For pullback and tensor, $r_F:G_F\to F_F$ and $r_T:G_T\to F_T$ are the specified natural identifications with the quotient/Roos models by [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison]. Their inverses are the defining $d_A$ by [lem-sf-primitive-reduction-transpose] and [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence]. Steps 2, 4 and 5 give $\sigma_F r_A(K^{(r)})=r_A(K)[r]\sigma_G$ for these realization identifications (here $r_A$ denotes $r_F$ or $r_T$, not the coefficient-system transpose). Multiplication by their inverses gives $\sigma_Gd_A(K^{(r)})=d_A(K)[r]\sigma_F$. For proper image, [lem-sf-primitive-reduction-transpose] identifies $d_A^{-1}$ with its defining whole-tower realization; the degreewise direct-image square of Steps 1-2 and the normalized total-limit square of Step 5 give exactly the same identity. These use the prescribed operation shifts, whose representative formulas are fixed by [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data].

source.place: Maps-used sentence, identifying the realized squares with the specified basic-operation comparisons.

proof.text: For open extension put $H(K)=\mathcal L\mathcal R(j_!K)$ and $F(K)=\mathcal LJ_j\mathcal RK$. The specified formula is $d_j^{-1}=\mathcal L(r_j)u_{j_!K}$ by [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Step 3 followed by Step 5 gives $\sigma_F\mathcal L(r_j(K[r]))=\mathcal L(r_j(K))[r]\sigma_H$. The actual unit, with these same reduction/total-limit shifts, satisfies $\sigma_Hu_{j_!K[r]}=u_{j_!K}[r]\sigma_{j_!}$ by [lem-pur-reduction-limit-shift-adjunction]. Substitution gives $\sigma_Fd_j(K[r])^{-1}=d_j(K)^{-1}[r]\sigma_{j_!}$. Inverting this square yields $\sigma_{j_!}d_j(K[r])=d_j(K)[r]\sigma_F$, the required identity. Invertibility of the unit here follows from the derived completeness of $j_!K$ explicitly asserted in the open-comparison node; no preservation of arbitrary inverse limits by $j_!$ is used.

source.place: Maps-used sentence, reconstruction-unit factor in the actual open realization.

proof.text: The quotient-model identifications are natural for all derived input morphisms and changes of good representatives by [lem-pur-quotient-system-flat-models] and [lem-pur-flat-roos-functor-descent]. The operation shifts have this independence by [lem-pur-basic-system-shift-resolution-calculus], the open comparison by [lem-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model], and the normalized limit bridge by [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. Consequently the representative squares above descend along these canonical identifications: applying any such identification to either route gives the same composite by naturality, and inverses give the assertion for roofs as well. Steps 6-7 therefore hold naturally in every derived input and independently of all resolutions. All compositions were made in the whole derived system and integral categories; neither cohomology nor evaluation is used to detect equality.
